title: How to Reduce Sodium Without Boring Meals
description: 6 simple swaps cut 420mg sodium per meal—without sacrificing flavor. Discover how to read labels and boost herbs, not salt.
perplexityQuestions: What should a 60-year-old eat in a day to get enough protein, fiber, calcium, and vitamin D?
How much protein do older adults need after age 65 if they’re trying to avoid muscle loss?
What are the best healthy snacks for seniors who have a small appetite or forget to eat?
How can a 70-year-old eat healthy on a fixed income without using expensive supplements?

competitorCoverage: The top-ranking articles mostly cover the same core themes: choosing nutrient-dense foods, increasing protein and fiber, staying hydrated, and limiting excess sodium, saturated fat, and added sugar. They also emphasize practical issues older adults face, like smaller appetites, budget constraints, meal planning, label reading, softer textures, and getting enough key nutrients such as calcium, vitamin D, potassium, and B12. A new article to compete should include actionable meal ideas, age-specific nutrient targets, barriers like chewing, appetite, or living alone, and clear guidance that is easy to apply in real life.
